title: Telling our story · Communications style guide
slide_intent: Teach writers to edit from the audience’s point of view. Specific words, structure and image choices influence what a reader can quickly understand.
strategic_value: Special Olympics contributors can use the same editing questions while telling stories from different programs.
demonstration: Green check marks identify guidance on choosing an entry point, writing inclusively and making information readable. Red crosses introduce pitfalls including jargon and crowded layouts.
practical_value: Review a draft for its intended audience, a specific athlete story, readable hierarchy and the language choices listed on the page.

content_islands.name: Purpose statement
content_islands.spec: Place the heading and its style-guide subtitle above the content, with a short bold introduction in the left rail.

content_islands.name: Editing checklist
content_islands.spec: Use two narrow columns of green check-mark items. Keep each instruction close to its explanation.

content_islands.name: Pitfalls
content_islands.spec: Put the red cross-mark items in a separate column at right so the reader can scan for problems during review.
